correctness.rationale: The 1993 primary Theorem 4 gives the base smooth one-line defect norm on real separable Hilbert spaces. Rotations preserve all properties and a common equivalence constant. Nonnegative norm-convexity remainders and a summable Lipschitz bound prove the exact Fréchet defect union for the finite/countably infinite positive series. The finite-head approximants have finite singular sets and dense Fréchet-smooth support functionals on every closed subspace by the 2026 Theorems 2/6 and Bishop–Phelps. Uniform norm and derivative bounds of (M+1)2^{-N}, dual norm comparability, derivative continuity at Fréchet points, and Baire avoidance of countably many closed lines give density for the limit norm on every closed subspace; Theorem 2 then yields hereditary MIP. Finite-dimensional and one-dimensional subspaces and countable-dense directions are covered without finite-to-infinite extrapolation.
